releases.notes:
## New

- Added support for **Minecraft 26.3.**
- **A heads-up before hosting.** If the world was last played on a different
  Minecraft version, or with mods you don't have installed, you get one
  screen that lists what changed before anything opens. Hosting on a newer
  version updates the world for good (friends still on the old version can't
  host it until they update); hosting on an older version can break parts of
  it; a missing mod takes its blocks and items out of the world. You decide:
  "Host anyway" or "Cancel". Hosting on an older Minecraft used to be refused
  outright; now it's your call.

## Fixed

- On 26.x, cancelling hosting at the wrong moment and hosting again could
  leave the game stuck on the loading screen until you restarted it.
- When Minecraft itself asks something before opening the world (for example
  "back up this world?" for a world from another version), pressing Cancel
  now takes you back to SharedWorld instead of leaving hosting half started.
- The button you just clicked no longer stays outlined after a step changes
  (most visible in the create world screens on 26.x).

releases.notes:
- e4mc is no longer a strict dependency of the mod. Users who have an alternative at hand, like Tailscale or RadminVPN, no longer need to install e4mc.
- Fixed a bug where if the upload to google drive failed when leaving a world, you could get stuck on that screen.
- Added support for Xaero's Minimap and World Map.
- Added support for Distant Horizons by not syncing LODs, which are huge and could fail the upload outright.
- Better error reporting if an S3 provider starts rejecting your credentials.

releases.notes:
- S3 bucket support. Much better than google drive storage in every way. Host it yourself or use a free S3 compatible provider to get much better performance, privacy (your email is not needed with S3!), not cluttering your Google Drive, and flexibility for users who like to host things themselves.
- Custom join addresses. E4MC is no longer a strict dependency. If you are having trouble with e4mc and something like tailscale, radmin vpn or just port forwarding works better for you, you can now just use that instead.
- NeoForge support.

releases.notes:
- New account screen to reconnect to Google Drive, disconnect, and a 'Delete all my data' button which fully deletes all your sharedworld data locally, on the backend, and Google Drive.
- Further secured PII (email and google drive token). It is encrypted on the backend and only full root access, not just a leakage of the database, would be required for a leak.

releases.notes:
- No more polling while connected
- Faster reactions to events (e.g. giving a user OP permissions now takes effect almost immediately).
- More reliable detection of network problems and disconnections.
- Caching responses, more responsive UIs
- Much more efficient backend
